Olga (eng-ml): quick flag: Zephyr->Orpheus import shows small but consistent drop after INT4 quant. Suspect tokenizer canonicalization + rotary index misalign.

Olga (eng-ml): numbers: LTQA-small fp16 acc@1=0.842 -> int4=0.833. Repro consistent across seeds.

Sam (mlinfra): can you paste a minimal repro?

Olga (eng-ml): minimal case: certain diacritics/ZWJ/soft-hyphen combos produce different token ids vs on-disk vocab. Example:
```
# disk vocab encode("naïve") -> [11234,903,44]
# runtime encode -> [11234,789,44]
```
Single-token id swap shifts kvcache indices -> rotary uses wrong phase. Quantization amplifies effect.

Kevin (eng-runtime): have you tried unicode normalization?

Olga (eng-ml): NFKC pre-normalize fixes most cases. With NFKC int4 acc@1=0.840. Remaining edge cases are ZWJ and soft-hyphen combos.

Luca (product): is NFKC safe as a shim for Hosted API?

Sam (mlinfra): short-term opt-in yes. Long-term we must canonicalize vocab/tokenizer and publish migration notes. Can't flip behavior silently.

Kevin (eng-runtime): runtime mitigation idea: probe kvcache alignment during early tokens and try rotary-offset fallback (+/-1) if misalignment detected. Low-cost and reversible.

Olga (eng-ml): I added an import-time checker to surface combining-char splits; will attach failing examples to the model package.

Sam (mlinfra): plan: 1) add opt-in nfkc compat flag in model metadata (default on for Dedicated/Private), 2) upstream tokenizer cleanup PR + migration guide, 3) lightweight runtime probe + rotary-offset fallback if probe rate > threshold.

Kevin (eng-runtime): I'll add a unit test blocking imports that produce >0.5% token-id divergence between canonical tokenizer and on-disk vocab.

ci-bot: started pipeline for branch nfkc-compat-shim (#432) :gear:

Sam (mlinfra): I'll run chair-bench across variants tonight and post results. Also adding an API header opt-in to preserve legacy tokenization for clients while we migrate.

Olga (eng-ml): noted. will push small repro + failing examples in PR. :thumbsup:
